title: Three-day fits gave no clear extra directional cooling with starting warmth at two California buoys in 2000-2023
abstract: We tested whether observed wind during the next three days had a stronger cooling link when coastal water started warm. We used 48 NOAA NDBC annual files at Bodega Bay and Monterey. April to September starts in 2000-2023 gave 7,546 station-days. Separate least-squares fits controlled wind strength, season, year and recent temperature change. The mean temperature by directional wind coefficient was +0.07468 C per 1 C higher start and 50 m2/s2 higher wind proxy. Its 95% three-year-block interval was -0.00065 to +0.14336. A negative coefficient would indicate extra directional cooling. A one-year-block interval was just above zero. Only 1.50% and 4.22% of the interaction variation remained after other controls. All fixed check point estimates were positive, but several intervals included zero. The main test gave no clear extra directional cooling from starting warmth. It did not show that strong winds fail to cool warm water. This extends prior past-wind forecast tests with realized future wind on overlapping data. It is not a forecast, an independent replication or a causal test. Two sites, correlated wind terms, missing data, sensor changes and omitted heat flux and currents limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate sufficient statistics, all draws, audits and figures permit inspection and reproduction. Raw and individual derived observations stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Main directional temperature interaction and the variation left after the other controls. Lines show paired three-year-block 95% intervals. A negative interaction would agree with extra directional cooling from a warmer start. Strength and direction have separate model terms.

All fixed checks for the equal-site directional interaction. Lines show paired three-year-block 95% intervals. Cases, horizons and model meanings can differ. The curvature row is the linear interaction at Q=0. These are related checks on the same archive.
